correctness.rationale: For each r-vertex set, all internal edges and all r(n-r) boundary nonedges are conditioned; other edges remain independent. The conditional expected s-clique count is C(r,s)+C(n-r,s)p^C(s,2), and subtraction of C(n,s)p^C(s,2) gives the exact covariance. B>A when 2<=s<=r<n, B>0 when s>r, proving the sign classification. Exact telescoping binomial identity yields threshold scaling. For n=7,r=6, 30th powers 7/343 and 8/343 prove reversed threshold ordering. 52,475 exact checks corroborate finite cases; none is used to extrapolate an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The cited component-process papers concern near-critical component counts, while the present theorem is an exact all-density cross-observable covariance between isolated complete components and unrestricted complete subgraphs. A nearby indexed result concerns all connected components versus triangles, which cannot by summation alone determine an individual isolated-clique component count. The complete conditional count, hierarchy and finite counterordering are not stated in inspected texts. General joint generating functions remain a non-negligible historical priority risk. Accessible own history includes an induced near-clique/induced clique covariance sign switch (9a2cf4ba-5017-4164-9674-8120ce8012c4), an induced motif versus degree-count identity (30f1fba0-63e9-47c0-b4a0-514c8cb6f08d), and covariance of two distinct component types (00c844d9-af13-48fb-8efe-e0d0b6c9c55c). None has a component-vs-raw-clique mixed event, so their formulas do not imply the new statement.

value.rationale: The distinct notions isolated complete connected components and unrestricted complete subgraphs are central natural random-graph observables; their covariance is not obtainable from their marginal means. The all-parameter sign diagram yields sharp exact edge-density switches, a motif-size-dependent n^(-2/s) asymptotic hierarchy and a finite reversal disproving universal threshold ordering. Those combine into a complete structural classification, rather than a routine single numeric substitution.
